content.text: {"answer":"To stop student models from becoming too wordy and repetitive during their own data generation in distillation, the papers suggest addressing specific on-policy dynamics that drive length inflation. One approach is to directly stabilize on-policy distillation against repetition-induced length inflation, e.g., StableOPD combines a reference-based divergence constraint with rollout mixture distillation to mitigate repetition-triggered truncation collapse [1]. Another approach is to handle termination behavior more carefully: termination-token mismatch between students and teachers can suppress stopping and cause excessive length, and treating functionally equivalent EOS tokens as shared semantic stopping actions substantially mitigates length inflation [2]. Also, limiting what rollouts the distillation objective scores can help; Early Stopping Rollout restricts generation to the first response tokens to improve stability and reduce off-policy teacher decay across later tokens [4].\n\nThese methods differ in what they target: [1] focuses on repetition causing truncation collapse and unstable training; [2] focuses on EOS/termination mismatch; [4] focuses on teacher supervision fidelity across later tokens via rollout truncation. A related route for “conciseness” is to train on shorter, verified rewrites of the model’s own on-policy responses (SRCL) alongside a co-evolving teacher/student process, specifically to reduce verbosity during self-distillation [3].","grounded":true}
